key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
engineering_relevance: Stabilizing self-assembled monolayer (SAM) interfaces addresses stress-driven adhesion failure that limits device durability under temperature fluctuations.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered SAM assembly.
Increase surface hydroxyl density to strengthen metal–oxygen coordination.
Add cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding for robust multipoint anchoring.
evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 cycles between −40 and 85 °C under ISOS-T-3 testing.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish manufacturing-scale reproducibility or long-term outdoor durability.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
